meaning: The instrument publisher's own English for the same numbered items. A parallel version rather than a translation of the administered string -- so where a local adaptation diverges from the original, this column stops corresponding word-for-word to the base field. Better wording, different provenance claim; that is why it is not merged with study_supplied.
This study's own deposit, supplement or paper carried an English rendering, and that is what ships.
No published English existed, so it was translated from the administered text by this project rather than by the authors. Requires an entry on the public issues page (ratified 2026-09-02).
Different fields came from different sources -- say which in the note.

A published English rendering that is neither this study's nor the instrument publisher's -- another study's printed table, typically chosen because it is the only open-access source carrying every item in one register. Published wording, so nothing is disclosed, but it is not the instrument original and may drift from it; name the paper in the note and say where it diverges. Added 2026-09-06 for gerber_2022_eas_temperament (irw#1970).

No _translated columns: the study was administered in English, so there is nothing to translate. NOT allowed on a text_source=translated_substitute row -- there English sits in the BASE fields, so where that English came from is exactly the question, and check_provenance.R fails a blank there (irw#1970, 2026-09-06).
The source states which response is correct -- an answer key in the codebook, deposit or paper. correct_response transcribes it.

No published key existed, so the correct answers were solved from the response data by this project rather than stated by the authors. Same class as machine_translation: it is IRW-generated content sitting in a content field, so it requires an entry on the public issues page (ratified 2026-09-03). Record in the note HOW it was derived and how well it reproduces, so a reader can judge it.
No correct_response, or the column is blank: the instrument has no correct answer (an attitude or frequency scale), so there is no key to source.
Every description of non-text content in item_text (a figure, graph, table, equation or diagram) was written by the source itself -- e.g. INEP's accessibility booklet for ENEM. Nothing to disclose.

At least one description of non-text content in item_text was written by this project, because the source described none. Allowed in item_text / item_text_translated only, always marked inline ('(AI-generated)' in English, the source-language equivalent in the base field), and NEVER in option_text: a generated label on a response category gets joined to responses and read as printed. Same class as machine_translation, so it requires an entry on the public issues page (ratified 2026-09-11, #1848). check_provenance.R enforces the marker rules against the __items.csv files beside it.
item_text carries no description of non-text content, or the column predates 2026-09-11.
